scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: A durable income engine is built mostly from the top of this table. The bottom rows are boosters you size small and expect to switch off. Blue-chip stablecoin lending, Borrower demand, High, Medium: moves with demand. Staking or liquid staking token, Network security rewards, High, Low to medium. Fixed-rate PTs to maturity, Locked at purchase, Fixed for the term, None until maturity. Curated lending vaults, Borrower demand in isolated markets, Medium, Medium. L.P. fees (major pairs), Trading volume, Medium, High. Funding or basis carry, Market positioning, Low to medium, High: can turn negative.
scenes.cap: A durable income engine is built mostly from the top of this table. The bottom rows are boosters you size small and expect to switch off. Blue-chip stablecoin lending, Borrower demand, High, Medium: moves with demand. Staking / LSTs, Network security rewards, High, Low–medium. Fixed-rate PTs to maturity, Locked at purchase, Fixed for the term, None until maturity. Curated lending vaults, Borrower demand in isolated markets, Medium, Medium. LP fees (major pairs), Trading volume, Medium, High. Funding / basis carry, Market positioning, Low–medium, High: can turn negative.

scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: Options premium, Volatility, Medium, High. Incentives or points, Protocol budgets, Low, Very high.
scenes.cap: Options premium, Volatility, Medium, High. Incentives / points, Protocol budgets, Low, Very high.

scenes.q: Why is funding carry low durability?
scenes.a: It depends on market positioning and can turn negative for long periods.

scenes.q: Which source gives a known rate for a set term?
scenes.vo: Question two. Which source gives a known rate for a set term? [[pause 4]] The answer: Fixed-rate PTs held to maturity.
scenes.cap: Question 2. Which source gives a known rate for a set term? The answer: Fixed-rate PTs held to maturity.

scenes.q: How should incentive income be treated?
scenes.a: As a temporary booster, sold on a schedule and not relied on.
